finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If T is a class with a non-trivial destructor that executes external commands based on its content, an attacker could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The type T might have a non-trivial destructor that executes external commands based on its content.

parsed.refutation_attempt: T is a template parameter, and arr is allocated by the Stack constructor with a size known at construction time (lines 19-22). The only data that could be untrusted are the T objects stored in arr via push() (line 35). However, the destructor (line 29) simply calls delete[] on the pointer returned by new, which only triggers the destructors of each T object but does not use any content of the objects to construct a command or invoke an OS-level function. Since the code does not pass any value from arr into a system call, and the pointer arr itself is not derived from external input, there is no path from untrusted data to a dangerous operation that is not neutralised. Therefore, the claim of OS Command Injection cannot be substantiated based on the provided fragment.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If T is a class that executes external commands based on its content when assigned, an attacker could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The type T might have an assignment operator that executes external commands based on its content.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any validation or sanitization of the input value before assignment. No checks exist; the assignment occurs directly if the stack is not full. There is no evidence of a concrete trigger in the code—vulnerability would only materialize if the template parameter T defines a dangerous assignment operator, which is outside the provided fragment.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If T is a class that executes external commands based on its content when returned, an attacker could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The type T might have a copy constructor or copy assignment operator that executes external commands based on its content.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Attempted to verify that the code fragment contains any call to an OS command execution function such as system(), exec(), or similar; no such calls exist. Checked for any sanitization or bounds checks before the pop operation, but the only check is the cnt>0 guard (line 41-42) which merely prevents out-of-bounds access; it does not neutralize side-effects from a type T's copy/assignment constructor. The reported vulnerability relies on the external definition of T, which is not present in the fragment. Thus the vulnerability cannot be confirmed based solely on the given code.
